item.title: She Used Her Fiancé’s Phone To Set A Fatal Trap
item.description: Antonetta Stevens used her fiancé’s phone to lure Ashley Bocanegra, 30, to a Georgia apartment complex in August 2022. Bocanegra died after an attack captured on video. Stevens and Janine Gonzalez later pleaded guilty to manslaughter and robbery and received 20-year prison sentences.

item.title: His Laptop Reopened The Clinton Email Investigation
item.description: Investigators examining former congressman Anthony Weiner’s contact with a minor found emails that revived the Clinton inquiry days before the 2016 election. That review did not change the FBI’s conclusions. Weiner pleaded guilty to transferring obscene material to a minor and received 21 months in prison in 2017.

item.title: The Reversed Video That Fueled Karen Read’s Defense
item.description: Mirrored police footage of Karen Read’s SUV became a flashpoint in her defense’s claim that she was framed for John O’Keefe’s death. Officers denied tampering with evidence. In June 2025, jurors acquitted Read of murder and related charges but convicted her of drunken driving.

item.title: The Email That Challenged Andrew’s Epstein Timeline
item.description: Former Prince Andrew said he cut contact with Jeffrey Epstein in 2010, but a reported 2011 email challenged that account. Andrew denies wrongdoing. Arrested in February 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office, he remains under investigation.

item.title: The Modeling Promises Behind Mike Jeffries’ Trafficking Charges
item.description: Prosecutors allege former Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries used promises of modeling opportunities to lure men into a sex-trafficking scheme. He has pleaded not guilty and was ruled competent to stand trial in August 2026.

item.title: He Posed As A Park Ranger Before Killing Four Campers
item.description: Herbert Mullin impersonated a park ranger before killing four campers during a California murder spree that claimed 13 lives in 1972–73. He claimed the killings would prevent earthquakes. Convicted of 11 murders, he received life sentences and died in custody in 2022.

item.title: She Said She Was “Doing All Right” The Day Before
item.description: Lindsay Clancy sought treatment for insomnia and anxiety before her three children died in Duxbury in January 2023. Her psychiatrist testified that Clancy reported doing “all right” the day before. Her defense argued postpartum psychosis; her 2026 murder trial ended in a mistrial without a verdict.

item.title: She Called 911 For Her Parents. Then Came Murder Charges
item.description: Sarah Grace Patrick called 911 after her mother and stepfather were found shot dead in their Georgia home in February 2025. Months later, she was charged with their murders. She has pleaded not guilty, and her trial has been delayed.
